title: Reading Drill — Reassembling a model ship — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Reassembling a model ship — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Cairnford, work on small loose pieces losing their original positions had already produced a small collection of assembly photographs. The museum model maker used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: parts assigned with confidence.

**B** The group kept labelled trays during repair for the new trial, which was planned to run for nine weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that earlier replacement parts should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
